hypothesis: The root cause is in the Bash completion script generated by Cobra. Bash splits words on COMP_WORDBREAKS characters (which includes `:` by default), so when a user types `local:/`, Bash sees `local`, `:`, and `/` as separate words. The generated Bash completion script needs to handle this by reassembling the colon-split word before passing it to the `__complete` command, similar to how other completion frameworks handle COMP_WORDBREAKS. The fix should be in the Bash completion script template (bash_completionsV2.go and/or bash_completions.go) to detect when the current word has been split on a colon and reconstruct the full word for `cur` and adjust `words` accordingly.
approach:
- Examine the Bash completion script templates in bash_completionsV2.go and bash_completions.go to find where `cur`, `words`, and `cword` are set.
- Add logic (similar to bash-completion library's `_get_comp_words_by_ref` or manual reassembly) to detect when `cur` has been split on a colon due to COMP_WORDBREAKS and reconstruct the full word.
- Specifically, after computing `cur` and `words`, check if the previous word(s) end with `:` or if `cur` was preceded by a colon-terminated token, and if so, prepend those segments back to `cur` and remove them from `words`.
- This is a well-known pattern: iterate backwards through `words` from `cword-1` while the previous word ends with `:` or equals `:`, prepending to `cur` and adjusting `cword`.
- Ensure the fix applies to both the V1 and V2 Bash completion scripts.
- Add or update tests in bash_completions_test.go to verify the generated script contains the colon-handling logic.
risks: Changing the Bash completion script template could break existing completions that do not use colons.
The fix must not affect zsh/fish/powershell completions which handle COMP_WORDBREAKS differently.
Users who have already sourced the old completion script will need to re-source it.
Edge cases: words ending with `::`, multiple colons, colons at start of word.
The reassembly logic must correctly adjust `cword` so the right number of positional args is passed to the completion function.
